_note: same scope as scope.json but without a rate wall, for tests that make many governed probes
_destructive_note: A SEPARATE fixture, deliberately. Tests that exercise DESTRUCTIVE capabilities — the BFLA prover changing another account's password with PUT, request tampering sending PUT/DELETE — need an engagement that authorised them, because GAP #15 made the web path refuse state-changing methods otherwise. Flipping the SHARED fixture instead broke two tests that depend on it being non-destructive (test_scope_authorisation_is_DISCLOSED, test_the_loop_seeds_BOTH_principals_once), which is the point: a fixture's authorisation is part of what it tests, so a test needing different authorisation needs a different fixture.
